title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 119
paragraphs: This was the penalty Astyages laid upon Harpagos. And about Cyrus he took thought, and summoned the same Magians who had given judgment about his dream in the manner already described. When they came, Astyages asked them how they had judged his vision, and they spoke according to the same manner, saying that the child must have become king if he had lived on and had not died before. Astyages answered them thus: “The child is alive and not dead. And while he was living in the country, the boys of the village appointed him king, and he performed completely all those things which real kings do — for he exercised rule, appointed spearmen of the guard and doorkeepers and message-bearers, and everything else. Now then, to what do these things seem to you to tend?” The Magians said: “If the child is still alive and became king without any arrangement, then concerning him be confident and of good courage, for he shall not rule again a second time. Some even of our oracles have had but small fulfillment, and that at least which has to do with dreams often comes in the end to a feeble accomplishment.” Astyages answered in these words: “I too, O Magians, am most disposed to believe that this is so, namely that since the boy was named king, the dream has had its fulfillment, and this boy is no longer a source of danger to me. Nevertheless, give me counsel, having well considered what is likely to be safest both for my house and for you.” In reply the Magians said: “To us also, O king, it is of great consequence that your rule should stand firm; for in the other case it is transferred to strangers, coming round to this boy who is a Persian, and we, being Medes, are made slaves and become of no account in the eyes of the Persians, since we are of a different race. But while you, who are one of our own nation, are established as our king, we both share in the rule and receive great honors from you. Therefore we must by all means take care of you and of your rule. And now, if we saw in this anything to cause fear, we would declare everything to you beforehand; but since the dream has had its issue in a trifling matter, we ourselves are of good cheer and exhort you to be so likewise. As for this boy, send him away from before your eyes to the Persians and to his parents.”
